directAnswer: Therapist SEO is the work of helping a counselling, psychotherapy or psychology practice rank in search so the right clients find it. For Canadian practices that means specialised service pages, a well-built Google Business Profile, and province-aware content that helps someone searching in their own city or province book with you.
intro: Therapist SEO is the work of making a counselling, psychotherapy or psychology practice easy to find when someone nearby is searching for help. It is not the same as ranking a shop or a restaurant. People looking for a therapist are usually anxious, comparing several practices, and reading for tone, specialisation and trust before they make contact. That changes what belongs on the page. Instead of pushing a single transaction, a good therapy site answers who you help, how you work, and what a first session actually looks like. Across Canada the search landscape also shifts by province: directory listings such as Psychology Today hold strong positions for generic terms, while more specific searches like trauma therapist, couples counsellor or child psychologist combined with a city are where an individual practice can genuinely win.
localInsight: Canada is ten provinces and three territories, and the words people use change from region to region. In Ontario and British Columbia, counsellor and psychotherapist are everyday terms; in Quebec, clients may search in French, and the Charter of the French Language means a French-language web presence is now a practical expectation rather than a nicety. Protected titles are regulated differently in each province, which affects the language a practice can legitimately use and how that should be explained to search engines. Therapist directories compete hard in the largest cities such as Toronto, Vancouver and Montreal, so the realistic opportunity for most practices is the long tail: modality, the population served, and location, expressed plainly and consistently across the website and the Google Business Profile.
localChecklist: A service page for each specialisation you actually offer, written for prospective clients rather than for a keyword.
A fully completed Google Business Profile with the correct primary category, services and service area.
Consistent name, address and phone details everywhere the practice appears online.
Location pages that describe the communities you serve without copying one page across the province.
Clear intake information: how to book, what happens first, and how fees work.
Trust content that respects client confidentiality and never publishes identifying client details.

faqs.a: Therapist SEO is search optimisation built specifically for counselling, psychotherapy and psychology practices. It combines technical fixes, specialisation-focused content, local visibility work and the Google Business Profile so that someone searching for help in your area can find and choose your practice.

faqs.q: How is therapist SEO different in Canada?
faqs.a: Canada regulates professional titles province by province, and in Quebec clients often search in French, so one national template will not fit every practice. A Canadian therapist SEO plan accounts for the province a practice operates in, the titles it is allowed to use there, and the language its clients search in.

faqs.q: Do you work with practices in every province?
faqs.a: Yes. We build pages for Ontario, Quebec, British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Newfoundland and Labrador, and Prince Edward Island, and we link each province page to the cities we cover inside it.

faqs.q: Why do directory listings outrank my own website?
faqs.a: Large directories such as Psychology Today have enormous authority and years of accumulated links, so they often sit above a solo practice for broad terms. The strategy is not to fight them for a generic word but to win the specific searches that describe your work, your population and your location.

faqs.q: Which specialisations can you write about?
faqs.a: We write only about what you genuinely offer. Common examples include anxiety, trauma, couples and relationship therapy, grief, adolescent and family work, and specific modalities. We do not invent services or clinical claims.
Only where they are appropriate and already public. Therapy marketing has to protect confidentiality, so we prefer aggregate feedback and practice-level trust signals over individual client stories.

faqs.q: How long before a practice sees results?
faqs.a: Local visibility usually starts improving within three to six months, with more meaningful gains between six and twelve. Timelines depend on your current site, the competition in your city, and how consistently content and profile work is maintained.
